chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad and another, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Ibn Muskān, from Badr ibn al-Walīd, from Abū al-Rabīʿ al-Shāmī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Indeed, the Imam, when he desires to know, is taught.

key_terms.الْإِمَامَ: the Imam, the divinely appointed leader

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the knowledge of the Imam عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the Imam عليه السلام is granted knowledge whenever he wills to know. It presents the Imam’s knowledge as divinely bestowed and connected to his station of authority.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad and someone else, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ayoub Bin Nuh, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Badr Bin Al Waleed, from Abu Al Rabie Al Shamy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Imam<sup>asws</sup>, whenever he<sup>asws</sup> desires that he<sup>asws</sup> knows (something), knows (it)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Muhammad and others have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ayyub ibn Nuh from Safwan ibn Yahya from ibn Muskan from Badr ibn al-Walid from abu al-Rabi‘ al-Shami from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following. “
Would the Imam (a.s.) like to know he would know.”
